Confusable pairs among the examination thresholds, plus continuation facts on the examiner's scoring that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
The 20/40 figure is the standard passing acuity, while a separate peripheral test measures side vision, so passing one screen does not cover the other. [A01]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable acuity versus peripheral; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A02
Side vision has two passing routes, 55 degrees in each eye or 85 degrees in a single eye, while 70 degrees combined is the floor below which no license is possible. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable standard minimum versus absolute cutoff; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A02
The 20/160 acuity cutoff applies only when both natural and corrected vision are worse than it; it is the point at which a license is impossible, not the standard passing level. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable cutoff versus standard; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A01
Both the Class F and the Class E written tests are closed book; the difference is that only the Class E test includes the commercial vehicle chapter. [A01]
Why it matters: group written test; confusable Class F versus Class E; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A01
An out-of-state license qualifies for the shortened vision and road sign route only if it is for the same type of license and is valid or expired less than 184 days. [A01]
Why it matters: group exam triggers; confusable transfer versus new applicant; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
Parallel parking and hill parking use the same curb-distance limit of no more than 18 inches. [A03]
Why it matters: group parking tasks; confusable parallel versus hill parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A03
Only parallel parking carries a time limit, two minutes, and only it uses a marked space, 25 feet long by seven feet wide. [A03]
Why it matters: group parking tasks; confusable parallel versus hill parking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A04
The point limit and the failure count are different numbers: losing more than 30 points fails a single test, while three failed tests trigger the Department authorization and extra training requirement. [A04]
Why it matters: group grading; confusable points versus attempts; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A04
A test can be failed outright without reaching the point limit, for example by breaking a traffic law or refusing an instruction. [A04]
Why it matters: group grading; confusable point deductions versus automatic failure; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A03
For the turning task you make a minimum of two right and two left turns. [A03]
Why it matters: group maneuvers; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A03
The intersection task includes making a full stop at the proper place at stop signs and yielding without blocking other traffic. [A03]
Why it matters: group maneuvers; prereq right-of-way rules.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A03
The examiner also grades whether you notice and obey traffic signs and signals throughout the drive. [A03]
Why it matters: group maneuvers; prereq road sign knowledge.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A02
After the examiner gives a direction, you are allowed enough time to check traffic and carry it out. [A02]
Why it matters: group test procedure; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A04
Results of failed driving tests are sent to the Department of Revenue, which then mails a letter requiring additional behind-the-wheel training. [A04]
Why it matters: group retests; continuation of the three-failure rule.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A04
The extra training after three failures must be given by an eligible driver, and you must hold Department approval to test before the next attempt. [A04]
Why it matters: group retests; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A01
The phone numbers for the Department and the Highway Patrol are printed at the back of the guide, and testing locations are also listed on the Highway Patrol website. [A01]
Why it matters: group test logistics; dynamic contact detail.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0020]
